# OpenAI refreshes Codex CLI for voice and agent oversight; the underlying features predate DevDay


By OpenTools Team


OpenAI's DevDay recap highlights voice steering and a new /agents view in Codex CLI. Its release history shows voice, subagents and worktrees arrived earlier, so the practical news is how those workflows are being brought together.


##


The DevDay change is a joined‑up terminal workflow


OpenAI used its[September 29 DevDay recap](https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap/) to present a refreshed Codex command‑line interface: developers can start and steer tasks by voice, use a new` /agents` view to delegate and track several tasks, and work with improved prompt editing, session resumption, worktrees and terminal readability. OpenAI says the update is available to all plans. For a developer juggling a long‑running fix and shorter investigations, the significant promise is less friction moving among those tasks in the terminal—not a newly announced model or a claim that each underlying capability first appeared today.


That distinction matters before a team rewrites its workflow around the announcement. OpenAI's[CLI guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli) already describes resuming a saved conversation with` codex resume` , delegating focused work to subagents and using an external editor for longer prompts. DevDay packages those pieces alongside voice and a clearer multi‑task view. The guide does not yet give a complete walkthrough of the recap's new voice and` /agents` interface, so the announcement should not be read as a tested instruction manual for every installation.


##


Voice and worktrees have a release history


OpenAI's[dated Codex changelog](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog) shows experimental` /voice` conversations in CLI 0.155.0 on September 17, with live transcripts and microphone controls on supported builds. In 0.156.0 on September 22, voice conversations became enabled by default, with an F8 toggle and` /voice settings` picker. Calling the DevDay recap the first launch of CLI voice would erase that staged rollout. The newer announcement instead emphasizes using voice to start and steer coding tasks as part of the refreshed terminal experience.


Worktrees followed a similar path. OpenAI's[September 9 release note](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11391654-chatgpt-business-release-notes) says CLI 0.154.0 added experimental starts and forks in separate Git worktrees. The[0.156.0 changelog](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog) says worktree support was enabled by default and the agent command center gained task‑status filtering and worktree‑session creation. Those dates make DevDay's worktree reference an improvement to a developing workflow, not the debut of Git isolation in Codex. A worktree lets a task proceed in a separate checkout; it does not, by itself, validate or merge that task's changes.


##


What the new agent view does—and what the docs still call it


The[DevDay recap](https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap/) calls` /agents` a new view for delegating work and tracking multiple tasks. OpenAI's current[subagents guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents) confirms that local Codex clients already run parallel subagent workflows, with a main thread collecting results. Its CLI‑specific instruction still says` /agent` to inspect and switch between threads. The two spellings appear in different current OpenAI documents; the guide does not establish that they are aliases or that the new view is in every installed CLI build. OpenAI’s[September 29 changelog](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog) lists 0.159.1 as the current CLI release and gives` npm install -g @openai/codex@0.159.1` , but its entry does not tie` /agents` to that version. Check the commands offered by the installed client when moving a team to the refreshed interface.


The practical gain, if the announced view is present, is visibility over delegated work. A developer can keep the main task focused while assigning independent exploration or checks and following their status. The same guide notes that subagents do their own model and tool work, so more parallelism can use more tokens than a comparable single‑agent run. That cost and review tradeoff still exists even when the command center makes delegation easier to operate. The[Codex tool record](https://opentools.ai/tools/codex) describes the underlying product and connects it to the[OpenAI organization](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) ; this CLI refresh is a dated update to that tool, not a second tool or an LLM benchmark release.
